Subject: MAP kickoff: technical introductions & evaluation plan for Velocity AI
Hi Lena / Mark —

Thanks again for the productive discovery last week. As discussed, I’ve attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out milestones and a suggested close timeline to get Velocity AI’s integration across Redwood’s Dedicated offering validated and contract-ready by the end of Q2.

Objective for this thread: lock the technical stakeholders and schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (Solutions Engineer + your Eng Lead + our ML Engineer) to align evaluation criteria, data access, and perf gates.
Proposed roles:
- Velocity Eng Lead: Mark Jensen — overall engineering owner, approvals for test data and VPC connectivity
- Velocity Procurement: procurement@velocity.ai — commercial steps and PO timeline
- Redwood AE: Sergio Alvarez — MAP owner and timeline tracking
- Redwood SE: Dylan Brooks — technical architecture and test harness setup
- Redwood ML Eng: Hiro Tanaka — benchmark targets, model compatibility checks
High-level timeline (draft):
- Week 1 (Mar 22–28): Technical kickoff + data access provisioned
- Week 2: Initial evaluation runs (functional correctness + latency baselines)
- Week 3: Perf tuning & quantization options; cost estimate finalization
- Week 4: Executive review & procurement sign-off
Attachments: Velocity_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP outline). Please review and suggest edits to the milestones or dates — this is flexible but we want a shared plan to keep things moving.
Can you confirm the best person on your side for the technical kickoff and potential time windows next week? Dylan and Hiro are available Tue–Thu 10:00–13:00 PT.
Thanks — looking forward to getting the team aligned.
Cheers,

Hi Lena / Mark — good to meet you virtually. Thanks for the quick turnaround on availability — Wed 11:00 PT works for Dylan/Hiro and me. I’ll calendar an invite once Sergio confirms.
Draft Technical Kickoff Agenda (60 min):
- Introductions & success criteria (10m) — confirm MAP goals
- Network/connectivity & security overview (10m) — SSO, VPC peering, IP allowlists
- Data for evaluation (10m) — sample size, data privacy, redaction needs
- Runbook for evaluation (15m) — what we’ll measure: latency p50/p95, correctness tests, throughput
- Next steps & timeline alignment (15m) — who owns what
Pre-kickoff asks from Redwood (to make the session productive):
1) A small representative sample (<= 500 items) of the evaluation data or a synthetic generator we can use — S3 link or shared Drive OK
2) Desired perf targets (e.g., p95 < 300ms at X concurrency) and any model quality thresholds
3) Any compliance constraints (SOC2, regional residency) or preferred deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
I’ve attached our evaluation checklist (redwood-eval-checklist.xlsx) to help structure the run. If you prefer, Hiro can sketch initial benchmark targets before the call once we have a sample.
Look forward to the kickoff — Sergio, can you send the calendar invite for Wed 24 11:00 PT and include a Google Meet + Drive links?
Thanks,

Hi all — quick note from the ML side ahead of Wed’s kickoff:
Helpful inputs if you can share before the call:
- Typical prompt/sequence length distribution (avg tokens per request and 95th percentile)
- Expected QPS or concurrency during evaluation runs
- Sample dataset (even anonymized) sized ~200–500 rows so we can run early correctness checks
- Any forbidden data categories (PII/PHI) so we can confirm redaction requirements

Preliminary considerations: if your workload has long context windows (>2k tokens) we’ll recommend a different performance profile and possibly a dedicated KV cache sizing. For initial evals we’ll run a small baseline on Redwood Hosted to validate correctness, then move to Dedicated for performance tuning if you want production-like numbers.
If procurement needs an outline of deliverables for the SOW or a short technical appendix, I can provide a 1-page summary after the kickoff.
See you Wed — Hiro
